headline: Meta acquires AI coding startup Conductor, teasing 'next interface' by early next year
summary: Conductor's founder teased "big, crazy plans" for a "next interface" by early next year, while its cloud service will shut down on November 20.
details: Meta has acquired Conductor, an AI coding startup that allows users to spin up software projects by deploying multiple agents into parallel workspaces. The acquisition was confirmed by Meta to TechCrunch and announced by Conductor's CEO on their blog.

Conductor's founder and CEO, Charlie Holtz, stated the company has "big, crazy plans" for a "next interface" and will have "something new" for customers by "early next year." He expressed excitement about working with Meta's AI leadership, including Alexandr Wang and Nat Friedman.

Conductor, founded in 2024, launched its core product last summer. Its agentic teams can be deployed in the cloud, locally, or via a user's phone, designed to help software engineers work on separate project parts in concert. The platform utilizes agents from major labs like Anthropic and OpenAI.

Holtz confirmed that Conductor's core features will continue to work until early next year. However, Conductor's cloud service will shut down on November 20, after which the company will begin deleting user cloud data.

Meta has been actively expanding its AI capabilities, having launched its own coding agent, Muse Code, in August. The company's Muse agents have seen significant adoption, surpassing 10 million users. This acquisition follows other AI-related purchases, including the viral agent platform Moltbook.

topic: qualcomm pivots to data centers as smartphone sales decline
headline_marked: [[Qualcomm expects data centers to be 30% of its business]] by 2029, amid sinking smartphone sales
headline: Qualcomm expects data centers to be 30% of its business by 2029, amid sinking smartphone sales
summary: Qualcomm projects its data center revenue will surge from $650 million in Q1 2027 to $15 billion by 2029, aiming for 30% of its total business as smartphone sales decline.
details: Qualcomm is making a significant pivot towards the data center market, anticipating it will account for 30 percent of its total business by 2029. This strategic shift comes as smartphone sales have reportedly tanked by around 20 percent compared to 2025.

During its Q4 2026 earnings call, Qualcomm laid out ambitious plans for its AI data center business. The company forecasts approximately $650 million in data center revenue during the first quarter of 2027, with projections to reach $5 billion by the end of 2027 and $15 billion by 2029.

Considering Qualcomm's total revenue for 2026 was $10.4 billion, these data center projections represent a substantial increase and a significant share of future earnings. The company has also announced partnerships with major players like Amazon and Meta to bolster its presence in this growing sector.

While not as aggressive as AMD, which targets over 80 percent of its revenue from data centers, Qualcomm's projections indicate strong confidence in the demand for AI-driven data center chips. This move highlights the broader industry trend of tech giants diversifying revenue streams beyond traditional consumer electronics.
